notes: Distinguish declaratory language (UDHR) from treaty obligations (ICESCR, CRC).
Never infer universal domestic applicability of a treaty; check States parties, declarations and dates.
These research cards need independent editorial validation and source snapshot capture before creation of KS/KA.

research_cards.statement_en: Article 26 of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights recognizes a right to education and provides for compulsory elementary education and free elementary and fundamental education.
Article 13 of the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights recognizes the right of everyone to education and requires free compulsory primary education for States parties.
research_cards.document: International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights
research_cards.jurisdiction: international treaty: obligations of States parties

research_cards.statement_en: Article 28 of the Convention on the Rights of the Child recognizes the child’s right to education and identifies measures for compulsory free primary education, accessible secondary education, attendance and reduced drop-out.
research_cards.document: Convention on the Rights of the Child
research_cards.jurisdiction: international treaty: obligations of States parties

research_cards.statement_en: The UNESCO Convention against Discrimination in Education was adopted in Paris on 14 December 1960 and entered into force on 22 May 1962.
research_cards.document: UNESCO Convention against Discrimination in Education
research_cards.jurisdiction: international treaty; participation varies by State

research_cards.statement_en: UNESCO describes State duties concerning the right to education as respect, protect and fulfil, and uses availability, accessibility, acceptability and adaptability as essential features.
research_cards.document: UNESCO State obligations and responsibilities on the right to education
research_cards.jurisdiction: International policy/legal explanation; jurisdiction-specific duties require confirmation

research_cards.statement_en: UNESCO Institute for Statistics SDG 4 framework includes distinct indicators for completion, out-of-school status, learning proficiency, parity and education finance.
research_cards.document: UNESCO Institute for Statistics SDG 4 Indicators
research_cards.jurisdiction: Global monitoring definitions; no country statistic imported

next_research_questions: How is availability, accessibility, acceptability and adaptability analyzed in education rights?
Which governance instruments implement the right in different jurisdictions and dates?
What evidence measures enrolment, completion, parity, inclusion and financing, and with what limitations?
